I downloaded the full Shambhala text of Enlightenment Unfolds and read Actualizing the Fundamental Point: it prints TO STUDY the buddha way is to study the self. To study the self is to forget the self. To forget the self is to be actualized by myriad things. When actualized by myriad things, your body and mind as well as the bodies and minds of others drop away. No trace of enlightenment remains, and this no-trace continues endlessly. The card's four sentences are that text exactly (the opening small caps are the book's section device). But that same book's Texts and Translation Credits says of this fascicle: Translated by Robert Aitken and the Editor. Revised at San Francisco Zen Center, and later at Berkeley Zen Center. So the publisher itself states that what it prints is a REVISION made after 1985, and the copyright-page line the verifier leaned on (Texts from Moon in a Dewdrop, copyright 1985 by San Francisco Zen Center, reprinted by permission of North Point Press) is a rights credit for the underlying work, not a statement that the two texts read alike. Both of the verifier's corroborating witnesses in fact credit the later printing rather than 1985: Terebess heads the text tr. Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi. Revised at San Francisco Zen Center, and later at Berkeley Zen Center; published (2000) in Tanahashi, Enlightenment Unfolds, 35-9. Earlier version in Tanahashi 1985 (Moon in a Dewdrop), 69-73. Upaya credits Enlightenment Unfolds (Boston: Shambhala, 2000), 35-9. Terebess also cannot bear weight on wording: its transcription reads No trace of REALIZATION remains where the printed Shambhala text reads No trace of ENLIGHTENMENT remains, so it is a third rendering, silently edited. Moon in a Dewdrop itself could not be opened this run: the archive.org copy (moonindewdrop00doge) is lending-restricted and its text returns 401, and the open secondary quotations of the 1985 page differ from the card in its very first clause, giving To study the Buddha Way capitalised. So the 1985 wording is unverified and there is positive reason to think it differs. Two further defects. The locator section 4 is a number no edition prints: Enlightenment Unfolds separates its sections with ornamental symbols and small-cap openings, Terebess supplied the bracketed numbers, so the card should say the fourth section. And a scope trap the editor must not walk into: the revision's copyright page reads copyright 1999 by San Francisco Zen Center, which keeps it inside the brief's pre-2000 line, but Terebess and Upaya both date the printing 2000, and a card citing 2000 is out of scope by the brief's own rule. Cite 1999, the copyright page I read. betterCitation names the book whose page was actually read; if the editor would rather keep 1985, the line cannot ship until someone opens Moon in a Dewdrop, pp. 69 to 73.
